department: Biomedical Sciences Program, Department of Veterinary Clinical and Life Sciences (College of Veterinary Medicine)

deadline.value: Applications are taken on a rolling basis, but to get department or Presidential Research Fellowship funding consideration you must be accepted by February 1, 2027.
deadline.quote: Applications are taken on a rolling basis | you must be accepted into the program by February 1 for the following fall semester

gre_subject.value: The page does not mention a GRE.

supervisor.value: You must identify a graduate faculty member willing to be your major professor before applying; identifying one does not guarantee acceptance.
supervisor.quote: Prior to applying for an MS or PhD in the Biomedical Sciences Program, a student must identify a graduate faculty member within the Department of Veterinary Clinical and Life Sciences to be willing to serve as their major professor

funding.value: Stipends depend on continued funding; the page does not say all or most admitted students are funded.
funding.quote: Graduate student stipends are dependent on the continued availability of funding

entry_route.value: A PhD can be entered from a BS (70 credit hours) or an MS (42 credit hours).
entry_route.quote: BS to PhD degree requires a minimum of 70 credit hours | MS to PhD degree requires a minimum of 42 credit hours

notes: Biomedical Sciences PhD is run by the College of Veterinary Medicine's Department of Veterinary Clinical and Life Sciences, which has its own MS/PhD admissions page. Its international English rule defers to the School of Graduate Studies, so the university English values apply. The deadline is a rolling date with the funding cut-off of February 1, 2027 recorded as time_sensitive. The page's application requirements list an overall GPA of 3.0 and prerequisite courses.
